messages.author: d3fbac5aabb27612
messages.subject: considering nugget effect
parts:
Dear INLA group,

I'm going to have nugget effect using SPDE for Binomial family. To do so, I consider
extra "iid" model in formula as follows:
mu<- 0+beta0+x +f(s, model="spde")+f(j, model="iid").

I'm in doubt I'm in the correct way or not.
If not how can consider the nugget effect in this model?

Thanks in advance for your help and time.

Leila

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] considering nugget effect
parts:
Hi,

if you want to add an iid effect to the predictor for each observation, and "j" is the observation index (1,2,3,...,n) then that looks like the correct formula, yes.

Finn

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] considering nugget effect
parts:
How spatially dense are the simulated observations? If they’re too far apart then it won’t be able to distinguish between the spatial field and the extra iid effect, and then the priors will be more influential. You probably need to go through your prior specifications and make sure they are reasonable for your problem.

Finn

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] considering nugget effect
parts:
I agree with Finn that you'll need to check the priors. How large is the estimated range compared to the distances in the data? The estimated sigma is huge for a binomial distribution. The code below illustrated how strong the random effect can be for different baseline values.

install.packages("inlatools", repos = "https://thierryo.r-universe.dev")
library(inlatools)
sims <- simulate_iid(sigma = 2.4)
plot(sims, link = "logit")

I considered this the same as the toy example in  " Advanced Spatial Modeling with Stochastic Partial Differential Equations Using R and INLA " book,
that is considered in the unit square.
pts <- cbind(s1 = sample(1:n / n - 0.5 / n)^2, s2 = sample(1:n / n - 0.5 / n)^2).
Also, I used the mesh,  inla.spde2.pcmatern and other thing same to this book.
For z ( nugget effect ), I considred the default prior for iid model.

Thank you for the package that you introduced. I've tried to install this but I got an error.
package ‘inlatools’ is not available for this version of R
A version of this package for your version of R might be available elsewhere,
see the ideas at
https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-patched/R-admin.html#Installing-packages


I tried for R versions 3.6.1, 4.0,  and 4.1.
What should I do?

On Monday, July 12, 2021 at 6:09:51 AM UTC-7 Thierry Onkelinx wrote:
I agree with Finn that you'll need to check the priors. How large is the estimated range compared to the distances in the data? The estimated sigma is huge for a binomial distribution. The code below illustrated how strong the random effect can be for different baseline values.

install.packages("inlatools", repos = "https://thierryo.r-universe.dev")
library(inlatools)
sims <- simulate_iid(sigma = 2.4)
plot(sims, link = "logit")

Op ma 12 jul. 2021 om 14:28 schreef Finn Lindgren <finn.l...@gmail.com>:
How spatially dense are the simulated observations? If they’re too far apart then it won’t be able to distinguish between the spatial field and the extra iid effect, and then the priors will be more influential. You probably need to go through your prior specifications and make sure they are reasonable for your problem.

Finn

On 12 Jul 2021, at 12:51, leila.b...@gmail.com <leila.b...@gmail.com> wrote:

﻿
Hi,
sorry for the late reply.
I'm in a simulation step. So, I can't find how can I simulate binomial data with spatial effect
to consider the nugget effect as well, and the result shows the nugget effect.
the linear predictor is
eta=1+b*x+u+z,
where "u" is simulated spatial effect using Matern covariance with nu=1, variance=5, kappa=7.
"z" is a simulated effect from Normal distribution with mean 0 and sd=0.1 to consider as a nugget effect.
The summary of result is
Model hyperparameters:
                                 mean              sd              0.025quant       0.5quant     0.975quant     mode
Range for i           5.26e-01        2.73e-01      0.192                 4.62e-01       1.23               0.364
Stdev for i            2.41e+00        8.74e-01      1.150                2.26e+00       4.54              1.994
Precision for z    1.85e+04       1.83e+04     1259.572           1.31e+04      66922.85     3436.917

As you can see the precision for z is big.

Thanks in advance for your help and time.
Leila



On Thursday, July 8, 2021 at 9:21:29 AM UTC-7 finn.l...@gmail.com wrote:
Hi,

not necessarily a problem; it seems to think that the data doesn't indicate that the extra iid component is needed, which may very well be true, in which case the large precision estimate is appropriate.

Finn

On Thu, 8 Jul 2021 at 15:14, leila.b...@gmail.com <leila.b...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi,
Thank you for your quick reply.
I did. The summary of results are here:
Model hyperparameters:
                                 mean       sd              0.025quant    0.5quant    0.975quant     mode
Range for i            4.24e-01 1.99e-01      0.173              3.79e-01   9.34e-01          0.308
Stdev for i             2.60e+00 7.72e-01     1.410              2.49e+00   4.41e+00        2.290
Precision for z     1.84e+04 1.82e+04   1251.757        1.30e+04   6.66e+04       3418.401

The precision estimation for z (nugget effect) is big and I don't know what's the problem

Leila

On Thursday, July 8, 2021 at 2:54:06 AM UTC-7 finn.l...@gmail.com wrote:
Hi,

if you want to add an iid effect to the predictor for each observation, and "j" is the observation index (1,2,3,...,n) then that looks like the correct formula, yes.

Finn

On Thu, 8 Jul 2021 at 07:40, leila.b...@gmail.com <leila.b...@gmail.com> wrote:
Dear INLA group,

I'm going to have nugget effect using SPDE for Binomial family. To do so, I consider
extra "iid" model in formula as follows:
mu<- 0+beta0+x +f(s, model="spde")+f(j, model="iid").

I'm in doubt I'm in the correct way or not.
If not how can consider the nugget effect in this model?

Thanks in advance for your help and time.

Leila
